correctness.rationale: For any finite poset P and downsets A,B the Heyting implication is A→B={p: downarrow(p)∩A⊆B}. Every minimal excluded p has all strict predecessors in A, so p belongs to C=A→B precisely if these predecessors lie in B. The equation (C→A)=A is therefore equivalent to S(A)⊆B, where S(A) is their predecessor boundary; other excluded points lie above a minimal one. The number of successful consequents is |J(P\S(A))|, giving the universal sum of failures. If P has a least element, each nonempty proper A has a failure B=empty; a strict length-three chain makes an additional failure, forcing rooted star for equality. If P has a greatest point, the coatom A=P\{g} has h−2 failures and comparable elements below g create an additional one, yielding dual star. Two-antichain-level formula follows by counting distinct proper-upper antecedents times proper-lower consequents. Independent direct Heyting pair evaluation checked a 3-chain (h,F)=(4,3), a rooted 4-element star (9,7), its dual (9,7), and the 2+2 two-level poset (7,9); all checked against the boundary failure criterion.

value.rationale: Quantifying how close finite non-Boolean Heyting algebras can be to satisfying Peirce law is the expressly studied degree-of-satisfiability problem. The exact boundary formula for arbitrary finite P plus sharp rooted/co-rooted carrier-dependent lower bound and rigid equality cases measure how qualitative near-classicality behaves; this is a motivated natural classification, not a trivial restatement of no-gap.
